arxiv-2301-12166.title: Heterogeneous Datasets for Federated Survival Analysis Simulation
arxiv-2301-12166.creator: Alberto Archetti, Eugenio Lomurno, Francesco Lattari, André Martin, Matteo Matteucci
arxiv-2301-12166.description: Abstract Survival analysis studies time-modeling techniques for an event of interest occurring for a population. Survival analysis found widespread applications in healthcare, engineering, and social sciences. However, the data needed to train survival models are often distributed, incomplete, censored, and confidential.

arxiv-2302-11128.title: Ignorance Is Bliss: The Screening Effect of (Noisy) Information Thanks: Previously titled “Looking the Other Way: The Screening Role of (Weak) Internal Monitoring”. We thank Judson Caskey (the editor) and two anonymous reviewers, Phil Dybvig, Paolo Fulghieri, Kebin Ma, Beatrice Michaeli, Sebastian P
arxiv-2302-11128.creator: Felix Zhiyu Feng, Wenyu Wang, Yufeng Wu, Gaoqing Zhang
arxiv-2302-11128.description: Abstract This paper studies the value of a firm’s internal information when the firm faces an adverse selection problem arising from unobservable managerial abilities. While more precise information allows the firm to make ex post more efficient investment decisions, noisier information has an ex ante screening effect that allows the firm to attract on-average better managers.

arxiv-2312-16795.title: Answers to Gould’s question concerning the existence of chorded cycles
arxiv-2312-16795.creator: Leyou Xu, Bo Zhou
arxiv-2312-16795.description: Abstract Answers are offered to Gould’s question to find spectral sufficient conditions that imply a graph contains a chorded cycle via signless Laplacian spectral radius. The conditions are tight. Keywords: Chord, Cycle, Chorded cycle, Signless Laplacian spectral radius Mathematics Subject Classification: 05C38, 05C50, 15A18 1 Introduction All graphs considered in this paper are simple and finite.

arxiv-2404-18863.title: PlanNetX: Learning an Efficient Neural Network Planner from MPC for Longitudinal Control
arxiv-2404-18863.creator: Jasper Hoffmann, Diego Fernandez Clausen, Julien Brosseit, Julian Bernhard, Klemens Esterle, Moritz Werling, Michael Karg, Joschka Bödecker
arxiv-2404-18863.description: Abstract Model predictive control is a powerful, optimization-based approach for controlling dynamical systems. However, the computational complexity of online optimization can be problematic on embedded devices. Especially, when we need to guarantee a fixed control frequency. Thus, previous work proposed to reduce the computational burden using imitation learning approximating the MPC policy by a neural network.

arxiv-2407-18011.title: HANNA: Hard-constraint Neural Network for Consistent Activity Coefficient Prediction
arxiv-2407-18011.creator: Thomas Specht, Mayank Nagda, Sophie Fellenz, Stephan Mandt, Hans Hasse, Fabian Jirasek
arxiv-2407-18011.description: Abstract We present the first hard-constraint neural network for predicting activity coefficients (HANNA), a thermodynamic mixture property that is the basis for many applications in science and engineering. Unlike traditional neural networks, which ignore physical laws and result in inconsistent predictions, our model is designed to strictly adhere to all thermodynamic consistency criteria.

arxiv-2410-05448.title: Task Diversity Shortens the In-Context Learning Plateau
arxiv-2410-05448.creator: Jaeyeon Kim jaeyeon_kim@g.harvard.edu, Sehyun Kwon shyun.kwon@samsung.com, Joo Young Choi jychoi@krafton.com, Jongho Park jjhpark@berkeley.edu, Jaewoong Cho jwcho@krafton.com, Jason D. Lee jasondlee@berkeley.edu, Ernest K. Ryu eryu@math.ucla.edu
arxiv-2410-05448.description: Abstract In-context learning (ICL) describes a language model’s ability to generate outputs based on a set of input demonstrations and a subsequent query. To understand this remarkable capability, researchers have studied simplified, stylized models. These studies have consistently observed long loss plateaus, during which models exhibit minimal improvement, followed by a sudden, rapid surge of learning.

arxiv-2508-19414.title: Even Heads Fix Odd Errors: Mechanistic Discovery and Surgical Repair in Transformer Attention
arxiv-2508-19414.creator: Gustavo A. Sandoval
arxiv-2508-19414.description: Abstract We present a mechanistic case study of a format-dependent reasoning failure in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, where the model incorrectly judges "9.11" as larger than "9.8" in chat or Q&A formats, but answers correctly in simple format. Through systematic intervention, we discover transformers implement even/odd attention head specialization: even indexed heads handle numerical comparison, while odd heads serve incompatible functions.

pmc-12562621.title: A Preliminary Study of Swell-Drying as an Innovative Process for Improving the Nutritional Quality of Dried Lucuma (Pouteria lucuma) and Dried Goldenberry (Physalis peruviana L.)
pmc-12562621.creator: Carmen Téllez-Pérez, Maritza Alonzo-Macías, Colette Besombes, Gastón Cruz, Daniel Marcelo-Aldana, Antonio Rodriguez-Zevallos, Karim Allaf, Anaberta Cardador-Martínez, Lucía Seguí, Joao Laurindo
pmc-12562621.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Lucuma and goldenberry are rich in bioactive compounds, and swell-drying (SD) can help preserve these properties. This study examined how SD impacts the nutritional quality of lucuma and goldenberry. The SD process involved the following: (1) initial pre-drying, with Interval Highly Active Drying (IHAD) for lucuma and Continuous Convective Airflow Drying (CCAD) for goldenberry, (2) a DIC treatment under an experimental design with 13 treatments, and (3) a final CCAD step.

pmc-12706849.title: Simultaneous electrochemical detection of Cu, Cd and Mn by nickel ferrite–cobalt ferrite bimetallic nanocomposite
pmc-12706849.creator: Zahid Ali, Jameel Ahmed Baig, Hassan Imran Afridi, Khalil Akhtar, Saima Perveen, Nadeem Raza
pmc-12706849.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The current study focuses on the synthesis of nanomaterials for fabrication of electrochemical sensors for the simultaneous detection of toxic metals, such as Cd, Cu, and Mn. Nickel and cobalt ferrite nanoparticles were synthesized by the sol–gel method and then combined by the green method to obtain a nickel ferrite–cobalt ferrite nanocomposite (NiFe2O4·CoFe2O4-NC) for electrochemical sensing of Cd, Cu and Mn.
